messages:
Alex P.: customer tickets 78942/78943 — heavy latency, intermittent wrong-region responses. they say requests from EU customers are landing in us-west and getting 300-800ms extra. Root cause preliminary: client app sets `redwood_region` cookie while also sending `x-region` header. Our router currently prioritizes the cookie. Can @eng-runtime confirm policy?
Maya K.: we saw similar case earlier but that was header vs query param. quick check — customer provided a curl repro:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "x-region: eu-central" \
  --cookie "redwood_region=us-west; path=/" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Response shows route served by us-west edge and latency ~460ms.
Jordan S.: ouch. their SDK sets cookie for persistence; when both cookie+header present we should prefer explicit header from client. current routing logic: cookie > header > query. That ordering was historical.
Ian Q.A.: any quick mitigation? customer on a timebox.
Alex P.: told them to clear cookies, add `x-region` header explicitly for now. They confirm it fixes routing.
Jordan S.: immediate fix: patch router to prefer header over cookie; low-risk config change. I'll open ENG-1245 and tag @eng-sre for rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy started for eng-runtime routing-priority-fix (PR 5387) — env: edge-canary — user: jordan.s — ts: 1765432110
Maya K.: also note telemetry shows ~0.6% of requests contain `redwood_region` cookie set by older SDKs — we should add a deprecation warning in SDK and an opt-out.
Ian Q.A.: thanks. I'll update the support ticket with repro steps + workaround and note the canary. customer asked for ETA; Jordan, please ping when canary looks good.
Jordan S.: will monitor canary for 30m then promote. If anything odd, rollback.
Alex P.: recorded in ticket 78942. closing loop when canary promoted.
